correctness.rationale: Reflection subgroups of order two force a covering problem: every dominating set must contain subgroups covering all \(n\) reflections, while any proper reflection-containing subgroup has at most \(n/p\) reflections. Equality uses the \(p\) subgroups \(H_{p,r}\). Their common rotation subgroup \(\langle a^p\rangle\) is nontrivial for composite \(n\), so the extremal constructions are cliques. The divisibility condition \(p^2\mid n\) is exactly the condition that \(\langle a^p\rangle\) also contains the order-\(p\) rotation subgroup. The paired value follows from even cardinality and explicit clique extensions. Exhaustive subgroup-intersection calculations for \(3\le n\le20\) agree exactly.

value.rationale: This is a complete infinite-family classification for two strengthened domination parameters on a classical algebraic graph. It pinpoints the prime-order obstruction, proves total domination equals the known ordinary value for every composite parameter, and shows paired domination is exactly the parity closure of that value. The result therefore captures a structural relationship among three natural domination notions rather than a one-off computation.
